newsitem.title: NORWAY: Lufeng oil vessel moves to Singapore for outfittin.
newsitem.headline: Lufeng oil vessel moves to Singapore for outfittin.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) ) said on Thursday work was underway at Singapore's Jurong yard to prepare the company's second multipurpose shuttle tanker, Munin, for oil production on the Lufeng field in the South China Sea.
The ship, which left South Korea's Samsung yard on July 4, will stay in Singapore for about three months while production modules and other equipment are installed.
The vessel is scheduled to be in position on the oilfield by late October.
Munin will have a production capacity of 60,000 barrels per day. It is owned by Statoil but will be managed by Norway's largest shipping company Bergesen d.y. ASA.
Lufeng is due to come on stream in December. An estimated 35 million barrels of recoverable oil will be produced through subsea wells in a template tied back to Munin.
